files.why: Framework-free AuditEntry entity (id, entityType 'invoice'|'appointment', entityId, actorId/actorName, occurredAt, field-level before/after changes) — the 'who/when/what' modelled as pure domain.
Pure helpers to summarize/format a change diff and sort/group entries for display, with no framework dependency.
Server-shape AuditEntryDto (snake_case, ISO dates, string ids) + zod schema; never escapes data/.
Maps AuditEntryDto <-> core AuditEntry (parse dates, normalize change shape); keeps DTOs from leaking upward.
Typed read: fetchChangeLog() / fetchChangeLogFor(entityType,id) over GET /api/audit-log via httpTransport, mapping DTO->core.
MSW handler for GET /api/audit-log plus the in-memory audit store and seed data, so the trail is real under the mock API.
View state that loads the change log (optionally filtered by entity) for the compliance screen.
Presentational table rendering one row per change: actor, timestamp, entity, and old->new values.
The compliance-facing page assembling the composable + table into a browsable audit trail.
The slice's only public surface: re-export routes, the read-model query, the AuditEntry type, and the mock handlers.
Add 'compliance' to the `slices` array (and 'audit'/'compliance' to domainNouns) so the toolchain and structure test recognize the new slice — CODEOWNERS-protected, needs architecture review.
Add the explicit `@slices/compliance` -> index.ts alias; the per-slice aliases are enumerated here (tsconfig's `@slices/*` glob already covers it, so tsconfig needs no change).
Concatenate `complianceRoutes` into the app route table (composition root).
Compose `complianceMockHandlers` into the MSW worker alongside billing/scheduling.
Add a nav link to the compliance change-log view.
Make the void-invoice mock handler append an audit entry when it applies the change, so recording happens at the (mock) server mutation boundary.
Make the reschedule mock handler append an audit entry (old vs new start/end) so appointment changes are captured server-side.

uncertain: Whether change-recording belongs in a new `compliance` slice at all vs. being purely a backend concern the frontend only reads. I modelled it as a read-only slice + captured writes in the existing mock handlers, because in a real system the server records the trail and the frontend just displays it. If the team already has (or plans) a backend audit service, the FE work collapses to just the read/display slice and the two mocks changes disappear.

The recording seam in this MOCK-only repo is genuinely awkward: the audit store is one shared server-side log, but billing/scheduling mock handlers live in different slices and the allow-list forbids data/->data/ cross-slice imports (only via index.ts). Having each slice's mock write into compliance's store would either couple slices or duplicate a store. In a real backend this is a non-issue; here it may push toward a shared mock/server seam I'm not sure the architecture wants.
Slice naming: I chose `compliance` (a business capability, matching billing/scheduling). It could instead be `audit`. Also unsure whether 'audit'/'compliance' should be added to `domainNouns`.

Whether billing/scheduling `data/mutations.ts` need to change to send actor context on the request. If the server derives the actor from the auth session, they don't; if the client must supply 'who', they do. Left out of the list pending the actor decision below.
questions: 'Who did it' — there is currently NO user/actor/auth/session concept anywhere in the codebase (grep found none). Where does actor identity come from? Is there an auth/session we integrate with, and should a shared or app-level current-user concept be introduced first? This blocks the 'who' requirement.

Is this recorded on the backend (preferred, authoritative) or must the frontend produce/submit audit entries? This determines whether the two mocks/mutations changes are real or just demo scaffolding.

Scope of 'every change': only the changes the app currently makes (void invoice, reschedule appointment), or all future mutating actions too? Should there be a general convention so new mutations are automatically audited rather than each remembering to log?
'What changed' granularity: full field-level before/after diffs, or just an action label (e.g. 'invoice voided')? Void has no obvious field diff; reschedule does.
Who consumes this — an in-app compliance view (as I assumed, with a route + nav link), an export/report, or an external SIEM/log sink? That changes whether the UI files are needed at all.
Retention/immutability/access-control expectations for a compliance record (append-only, who may view it) — relevant if any of this is enforced client-side.
